title.zh: 卷460 列傳二百四十七 左宝贵弟：宝贤 永山 邓世昌 刘步蟾 林泰曾 戴宗骞
title.en: Volume 460 Biographies 247: Zuo Baogui younger brother: Bao Xian, Yong Shan, Deng Shichang, Liu Buchan, Lin Taiceng, Dai Zongqian
title.raw: 卷460 列傳二百四十七 左宝贵弟：宝贤 永山 邓世昌 刘步蟾 林泰曾 戴宗骞

sentences.zh: 列傳二百四十七

translations.literal: Biographies 247
translations.idiomatic: Biography 247

sentences.zh: 左寶貴弟寶賢等永山鄧世昌劉步蟾林泰曾等戴宗騫

translations.literal: Zuo Baogui; his younger brothers Bao Xian and the like; Yong Shan; Deng Shichang; Liu Buchan; Lin Taiceng and others; Dai Zongqian
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Baogui; his younger brothers Bao Xian and others; Yong Shan; Deng Shichang; Liu Buchan; Lin Taiceng and others; Dai Zongqian

sentences.zh: 左寶貴，字冠廷，山東費人。

translations.literal: Zuo Baogui, style name Guanting, was a man of Fei in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Baogui, whose style name was Guanting, was a native of Fei in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，隸江南軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xianfeng reign, he was enrolled in the Jiangnan Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Xianfeng era he joined the Jiangnan Army.

sentences.zh: 嘗令當前敵，陣既接，旗兵中砲，殪，寶貴持其幟衝鋒入，大捷，繇是知名。

translations.literal: He was once ordered to face the enemy in the front rank. Once the formations had joined battle, the banner soldier bearing the standard was struck by cannon fire and killed. Baogui seized his banner and charged in at the head of the assault, winning a great victory, and from this became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he was ordered to take the front rank against the enemy. When the lines met, the standard-bearer was killed by artillery fire. Baogui seized the flag and led a charge, winning a decisive victory and making his name known from that day on.

sentences.zh: 獲苗沛霖，克金陵，頻有功。

translations.literal: He captured Miao Peilin, took Jinling, and repeatedly distinguished himself.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Miao Peilin, helped take Nanjing, and won distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 後以游擊從僧格林沁討捻，積勳至副將。

translations.literal: Later, as a guerrilla officer he followed Sengge Rinchen in suppressing the Nian rebels, accumulating merit until he reached the rank of deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as a guerrilla officer under Sengge Rinchen in campaigns against the Nian rebels, rising through accumulated merit to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，尚書崇實巡視奉天、吉林，奏自隨。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangxu reign, Minister Chongshi inspected Fengtian and Jilin and memorialized that Baogui accompany him on his own initiative.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxu reign, Minister Chongshi toured Fengtian and Jilin and had Baogui accompany him at his own request.

sentences.zh: 既至，斬高希珍於土門，誅宋三好於石砬子。

translations.literal: After their arrival, he beheaded Gao Xizhen at Tumen and executed Song Sanhao at Shi'azi.
translations.idiomatic: Once they arrived, he beheaded Gao Xizhen at Tumen and executed Song Sanhao at Shi'azi.

sentences.zh: 邊外東北廟溝金宮四構黨圖大舉，复捕治之，餘燼悉平，賜號鏗色巴圖魯，晉記名提督。

translations.literal: Beyond the border to the northeast, at Miaogou, Jingong, and Sigou, a party plotted a large rising; he again captured and punished them, and the remaining embers were all extinguished. He was granted the title Kense Batür, and was promoted to named reserve grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: In the borderlands northeast of the passes, conspirators at Miaogou, Jingong, and Sigou planned a major uprising; he suppressed them as well until every last remnant was extinguished. He received the honorific title Kense Batür and was entered on the rolls for promotion to grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 授高州鎮總兵，仍留奉天。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander of the Gaozhou garrison but remained in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commander of the Gaozhou garrison while continuing to serve in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 平朝陽教匪，賞黃馬褂、雙眼花翎，駐瀋陽。

translations.literal: He quelled the religious rebels in Chaoyang, and was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket and double-eyed peacock plumes; he was stationed at Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: He put down the sectarian rebels in Chaoyang, was awarded the yellow riding jacket and double-eyed peacock feathers, and was garrisoned at Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 二十年，朝鮮亂起，日本進兵。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, turmoil broke out in Korea and Japan sent troops.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 unrest erupted in Korea and Japan marched troops in.

sentences.zh: 朝議既決戰，衛汝貴、馬玉昆、丰紳阿各率所部往御之，寶貴自奉天來會，是為四大軍。

translations.literal: Once the court had decided on war, Wei Rugui, Ma Yukun, and Fengshen'a each led their commands to resist the enemy. Baogui came from Fengtian to join them—this was the Four Great Armies.
translations.idiomatic: After the court resolved on war, Wei Rugui, Ma Yukun, and Fengshen'a each marched their forces to meet the invaders. Baogui came down from Fengtian to join them, forming what were called the four great armies.

sentences.zh: 慮海道梗，乃繞道自遼東行，渡鴨綠江入平壤。

translations.literal: Fearing that the sea route would be blocked, they took a detour through Liaodong, crossed the Yalu River, and entered Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the sea lanes would be cut, they marched overland through Liaodong, crossed the Yalu, and entered Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 是時葉志超虛飾戰胜狀，電李鴻章入告，遂拜總統諸軍命。

translations.literal: At that time Ye Zhichao had falsely reported a victory; he telegraphed Li Hongzhang to report it, and was thereupon appointed commander-in-chief of all the armies.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ye Zhichao had inflated reports of victory and wired Li Hongzhang; on that basis he was appointed supreme commander of the allied forces.

sentences.zh: 於是汝貴、玉昆軍南門外大同江，志超部將江自康軍北門外小山，寶貴任城守。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wei Rugui and Ma Yukun's armies were at the southern gate outside the city on the Taedong River, Ye Zhichao's subordinate Jiang Zikang's force was at the hill outside the northern gate, and Baogui was charged with defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Rugui and Ma Yukun held the southern approaches along the Taedong River, Ye Zhichao's lieutenant Jiang Zikang held the hill north of the city, and Baogui was assigned to hold the walls.

sentences.zh: 未止舍，日軍猝至，寶貴與丰紳阿擊卻之。

translations.literal: Before they had even pitched camp, Japanese troops arrived suddenly; Baogui and Fengshen'a drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: They had barely encamped when Japanese troops struck; Baogui and Fengshen'a beat them off.

sentences.zh: 敵退龍岡，分道來攻，又敗之。

translations.literal: The enemy withdrew to Longgang; they came to attack by separate routes, and were defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fell back to Longgang and attacked again along several routes, only to be defeated once more.

sentences.zh: 志超乃聚全軍為嬰城計。

translations.literal: Zhichao then gathered the entire army into a plan of defending the city as if besieged within.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichao then concentrated the whole army on a purely defensive, hold-the-city strategy.

sentences.zh: 時寶貴扼玄武門，日軍大隊至。

translations.literal: At that time Baogui held the Xuanwu Gate; a large Japanese force arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Baogui was holding the Xuanwu Gate when a major Japanese column arrived.

sentences.zh: 志超將潰圍北歸，寶貴不從，以兵守志超勿令逸。

translations.literal: Zhichao was about to break out of the encirclement and retreat north, but Baogui would not agree, and posted troops to prevent Zhichao from fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhichao intended to break out northward, but Baogui refused and stationed men to keep him from slipping away.

sentences.zh: 寶貴狃於捕馬賊之功，頗輕敵。

translations.literal: Baogui had grown overconfident from his successes in hunting down mounted bandits and rather looked down on the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Success against mounted bandits had made Baogui overconfident, and he tended to underestimate the foe.

sentences.zh: 日軍轝砲散置山巔，諜者以告，若弗聞。

translations.literal: The Japanese had scattered their field guns on the hilltops; spies reported this, but he seemed not to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese field guns were deployed on the heights; scouts reported it, yet he paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 登城指麾，中砲踣，猶能言，及城下，始殞。

translations.literal: He mounted the wall to direct operations, was struck by cannon fire and fell; he could still speak, but only when he reached the foot of the wall did he die.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed the wall to command the fight, was hit by shellfire and fell; he could still speak, but died only after being carried below the wall.

sentences.zh: 其部將負屍開城走，遇日軍，又棄之，於是諸軍皆潰。

translations.literal: His subordinate generals carried his corpse and opened the gates to flee; they met Japanese troops and abandoned the body, whereupon all the armies collapsed in rout.
translations.idiomatic: His officers bore his body out through the opened gates, met Japanese troops, and abandoned the corpse; the armies then broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太子少保，諡忠壯，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，子國楫襲。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, given the posthumous title Zhongzhuang, granted the hereditary office of Commandant of Cavalry with one additional Yunqiwei, and his son Guoji inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: On report of his death he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, honored with the posthumous name Zhongzhuang, granted a hereditary Commandant of Cavalry plus one Yunqiwei, and his son Guoji succeeded to the rank.

sentences.zh: 弟寶賢、寶清先後於直隸、奉天剿匪陣亡。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Bao Xian and Bao Qing successively died in battle while suppressing bandits in Zhili and Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Bao Xian and Bao Qing were killed in turn fighting bandits in Zhili and Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 永山，袁氏，漢軍正白旗人，黑龍江駐防，吉林將軍富明阿子，黑龍江將軍壽山弟。

translations.literal: Yong Shan, of the Yuan clan, was a man of the Plain White Banner of the Hanjun, garrisoned at Heilongjiang; he was the son of Jilin General Fuming'a and the younger brother of Heilongjiang General Shoushan.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Shan, of the Yuan clan, belonged to the Plain White Banner of the Hanjun and was stationed in Heilongjiang; he was the son of Jilin General Fuming'a and younger brother of Heilongjiang General Shoushan.

sentences.zh: 以廕授侍衛，歸東三省練軍。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he was appointed an imperial bodyguard and returned to the training army of the Three Eastern Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service by hereditary appointment as an imperial bodyguard and joined the training army of the Three Eastern Provinces.

sentences.zh: 中日戰起，從將軍依克唐阿軍，率黑龍江騎旅駐摩天嶺。

translations.literal: When the Sino-Japanese War broke out, he followed General Yiketang'a's army, leading the Heilongjiang cavalry brigade stationed at Motian Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: When war with Japan began he served under General Yiketang'a, commanding the Heilongjiang cavalry brigade at Motian Ridge.

sentences.zh: 永山臨敵輒深入，為士卒先。

translations.literal: Whenever Yong Shan faced the enemy he plunged deep into the fight, going before the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In battle Yong Shan always pushed far ahead, leading from the front.

sentences.zh: 與日軍戰數有功，連殲其將。

translations.literal: He fought the Japanese several times with merit, repeatedly destroying their generals.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the Japanese repeatedly with success and killed several of their commanders in succession.

sentences.zh: 既克龍灣，乘勝渡草河，規鳳凰，依克唐阿策襲其城，檄永山為軍鋒，偕壽山分率馬步隊深入攻之。

translations.literal: After Longwan was taken, he crossed the Cao River in pursuit of victory and aimed at Fengcheng; Yiketang'a planned a surprise attack on the city and ordered Yong Shan as the army's vanguard, joining Shoushan in leading cavalry and infantry deep in the assault.
translations.idiomatic: After Longwan fell he crossed the Cao River in pursuit and set his sights on Fengcheng; Yiketang'a devised a surprise on the city and named Yong Shan vanguard, while he and Shoushan led horse and foot in a deep strike.

sentences.zh: 抵一面山，距城八里，張左右翼，各據一坡以待。

translations.literal: They reached Yimian Hill, eight li from the city, deployed left and right wings, and each occupied a slope to await the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Yimian Hill eight li from the city, formed left and right wings, and each wing held a hill to await attack.

sentences.zh: 永山為右翼，尤得地勢。

translations.literal: Yong Shan commanded the right wing and especially held the superior ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Shan held the right wing, which enjoyed the better terrain.

sentences.zh: 敵作散隊，伍伍什什冒死前，復以大隊橫沖我左翼。

translations.literal: The enemy advanced in open order, in scattered squads risking death to press forward, then sent a large column to charge straight into our left wing.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese came on in open skirmish lines, small groups pressing forward at all costs, then threw a large force in a frontal rush against our left.

sentences.zh: 左翼潰，右翼亦不支，乃相繼退。

translations.literal: The left wing collapsed; the right wing could not hold either, and they retreated in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The left wing broke; the right could not stand, and both wings fell back one after another.

sentences.zh: 永山獨為殿，遇伏，連受槍傷，洞胸踣，復強起督戰，大呼殺賊而逝。

translations.literal: Yong Shan alone brought up the rear; he met an ambush, was repeatedly shot, a bullet pierced his chest and he fell; he forced himself up again to direct the fight, shouted to kill the enemy, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Shan alone covered the retreat, walked into an ambush, and took repeated gunfire; a shot through the chest dropped him, yet he rose again to command, crying to slay the foe until he expired.

sentences.zh: 事聞，諡壯愍，予建祠奉天。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, he was given the posthumous title Zhuangmin and a temple was ordered built for him in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: On report of his death he received the posthumous name Zhuangmin and a shrine was ordered erected in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 鄧世昌，字正卿，廣東番禺人。

translations.literal: Deng Shichang, style name Zhengqing, was a man of Panyu in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Shichang, whose style name was Zhengqing, was a native of Panyu in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 少有幹略，嘗從西人習布算術。

translations.literal: In youth he had ability and resourcefulness, and once studied Western arithmetic with foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he showed talent and initiative and had studied Western mathematics with foreigners.

sentences.zh: 既長，入水師學堂，精測量、駕駛。

translations.literal: When grown, he entered the naval academy and mastered surveying and navigation.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he entered the naval academy and mastered surveying and ship handling.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，管海東雲艦，徼循海口。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu he commanded the coastal patrol ship Hai Dongyun, patrolling the mouth of the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxu reign he commanded the patrol vessel Hai Dongyun on coastal duty.

sentences.zh: 日本窺台灣，扼澎湖、基隆諸隘，補千總，調管振威艦。

translations.literal: When Japan eyed Taiwan and seized the passes at Penghu and Keelung, he was promoted to company commander and transferred to command the Zhenwei.
translations.idiomatic: When Japan cast its eye on Taiwan and seized Penghu and Keelung, he was promoted to company commander and given the Zhenwei.

sentences.zh: 以捕海盜，遷守備。

translations.literal: For capturing pirates he was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to garrison commander for capturing pirates.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章治海軍，高其能，調北洋。

translations.literal: When Li Hongzhang organized the navy, he valued Shichang's ability and transferred him to the Beiyang Fleet.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang, building the navy, prized his ability and moved him to the Beiyang Fleet.

sentences.zh: 從丁汝昌赴英購鐵艦，益詳練海戰術。

translations.literal: He followed Ding Ruchang to England to purchase ironclads and became still more expert in naval tactics.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Ding Ruchang to England to buy ironclads and grew thoroughly versed in naval warfare.

sentences.zh: 八年，朝鮮內亂，復從汝昌泊仁川，為吳長慶陸軍後距。

translations.literal: In the eighth year internal disorder broke out in Korea; he again followed Ruchang to anchor at Inchon as rear support for Wu Changqing's land force.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882, when Korea was torn by internal strife, he again followed Ruchang to Inchon as naval cover for Wu Changqing's army ashore.

sentences.zh: 事寧，遷游擊，賜號勃勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was promoted to guerrilla officer and granted the title Boyong Batür.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored he was made guerrilla officer and granted the title Boyong Batür.

sentences.zh: 管揚威快艦，往來天津、朝鮮；

translations.literal: He commanded the fast cruisers Yangwei and made runs between Tianjin and Korea;
translations.idiomatic: He took command of the fast cruiser Yangwei and shuttled between Tianjin and Korea;

sentences.zh: 冬寒冰沍，巡視台、廈海防。

translations.literal: in winter, when ice froze hard, he patrolled the defenses of Taiwan and Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: in winter, when the seas froze, he inspected the coastal defenses of Taiwan and Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 尋充經遠、致遠、靖遠、濟遠四船營務處，兼致遠管帶。

translations.literal: Soon he was placed in charge of the depot for the four ships Jingyuan, Zhiyuan, Jingyuan (second), and Jiyuan, and also commanded the Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made depot officer for the Jingyuan, Zhiyuan, Jingyuan, and Jiyuan and given command of the Zhiyuan as well.

sentences.zh: 十四年，台灣生番畔，以副將從汝昌往討。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when the Taiwan aborigines rebelled, he followed Ruchang as deputy commander to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1888, when Taiwan's indigenous peoples rose, he went as deputy commander under Ruchang to subdue them.

sentences.zh: 戰埤南，毀其碉寨，擢總兵。

translations.literal: He fought at Beinan, destroyed their stockades, and was promoted to commander.
translations.idiomatic: At Beinan he destroyed their fortifications and was promoted to commander.

sentences.zh: 時定海軍經制，借補中軍副將，而以汝昌為提督，其左右翼總兵則閩人林泰曾、劉步蟾也。

translations.literal: At that time the permanent organization of the navy was fixed; he was lent in as deputy commander of the central squadron, while Ruchang became admiral and the wing commanders were the Fujian men Lin Taiceng and Liu Buchan.
translations.idiomatic: When the navy's permanent establishment was set, he was lent in as central squadron deputy commander; Ruchang became admiral, with the Fujian natives Lin Taiceng and Liu Buchan as wing commanders.

sentences.zh: 汝昌故不習海戰，威令不行。

translations.literal: Ruchang had never been versed in naval warfare and his authority did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Ruchang had never mastered naval combat and could not enforce discipline.

sentences.zh: 獨世昌以粵人任管駕，非時不登岸，閩人咸嫉之。

translations.literal: Only Shichang, a Cantonese holding command of navigation, unless absolutely necessary did not go ashore, and the Fujian men all envied him.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang alone, a Cantonese in charge of sailing, scarcely left his ship except when he must, and the Fujian officers resented him.

sentences.zh: 二十年夏，日侵朝，絕海道。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twentieth year Japan invaded Korea and cut the sea routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 1894 Japan invaded Korea and severed the sea lanes.

sentences.zh: 鴻章令濟遠、廣乙兩船赴牙山，遇日艦，先擊，廣乙受殊傷；

translations.literal: Hongzhang ordered the Jiyuan and Guangyi to proceed to Asan; they met Japanese warships and opened fire first; the Guangyi was gravely damaged;
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang sent the Jiyuan and Guangyi to Asan; they met Japanese ships and fired first; the Guangyi was badly mauled;

sentences.zh: 轟濟遠，都司沈壽昌，守備楊建章、黃承勳中砲死。

translations.literal: shells struck the Jiyuan; Battalion Commander Shen Shouchang and garrison commanders Yang Jianzhang and Huang Chengxun were killed by cannon fire.
translations.idiomatic: the Jiyuan was shelled; Battalion Commander Shen Shouchang and garrison commanders Yang Jianzhang and Huang Chengxun were killed by gunfire.

sentences.zh: 濟遠逃，日艦追之，管帶方柏謙豎白幟，追益亟，有水手發砲擊之，折日艦了樓，柏謙虛張胜狀，退塞威海東西兩口。

translations.literal: The Jiyuan fled; Japanese ships pursued; Commander Fang Boyian hoisted a white flag, the pursuit grew fiercer, a sailor fired and struck the Japanese ship's superstructure, Boyian falsely claimed victory, and withdrew to block the eastern and western mouths of Weihai.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiyuan fled with Japanese ships in pursuit; her commander Fang Boyian ran up a white flag, yet when pursuit intensified a sailor fired and damaged a Japanese superstructure; Boyian reported a false victory and withdrew to seal Weihai's eastern and western entrances.

sentences.zh: 世昌憤欲進兵，汝昌尼其行，不果。

translations.literal: Shichang was furious and wished to advance, but Ruchang restrained him and it came to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang burned to attack, but Ruchang held him back and the chance was lost.

sentences.zh: 已而日艦集大連灣，窺金州，我國海軍乃大發，泊鴨綠江大東溝，以鐵艦十當敵艦十有二。

translations.literal: Before long Japanese ships gathered at Dalian Bay and probed Jinzhou; our navy then sortied in force and anchored at Dadonggou on the Yalu, pitting ten ironclads against twelve enemy vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Japanese squadrons massed at Dalian Bay and reconnoitered Jinzhou; the Chinese fleet sailed out in strength and anchored at Dadonggou on the Yalu with ten ironclads against twelve Japanese ships.

sentences.zh: 汝昌乘定遠居中，列諸船左右張兩翼。

translations.literal: Ruchang rode the Dingyuan in the center, arraying the other ships left and right in two wings.
translations.idiomatic: Ruchang took the Dingyuan at the center and drew the fleet up in wings to either side.

sentences.zh: 日艦魚貫進，據上風，汝昌令轟擊，距遠不能中。

translations.literal: The Japanese ships advanced in single file, held the windward position; Ruchang ordered shelling, but at such distance they could not hit.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese ships came on in column with the weather gauge; Ruchang ordered fire, but at long range the shots fell short.

sentences.zh: 日艦小，運棹靈，倏分倏合，彈雨坌集，定遠被震，大纛僕。

translations.literal: The Japanese ships were small and their oars nimble; they split and joined again in an instant; shot fell like rain; the Dingyuan was shaken and the great standard toppled.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese vessels were smaller and handier; they divided and re-formed at will; shot poured in; the Dingyuan shuddered and her mainmast banner fell.

sentences.zh: 世昌見帥旗沒，慮軍心搖，亟取致遠纛豎之。

translations.literal: Shichang saw the commander's flag gone and feared the troops' hearts would waver; he quickly took the Zhiyuan's standard and raised it.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the admiral's flag down, Shichang feared morale would crack and at once hoisted the Zhiyuan's banner in its place.

sentences.zh: 戰良久，定遠擊沉其西京丸，我之超勇毀焉。

translations.literal: After long fighting the Dingyuan sank the Japanese Saikyō Maru, while our Chaoyong was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: After hours of combat the Dingyuan sank the Japanese Saikyō Maru, but our Chaoyong was lost.

sentences.zh: 世昌乘致遠，最猛鷙，與日艦吉野浪速相當，吉野，日艦之中堅也。

translations.literal: Shichang rode the Zhiyuan, the fiercest of all; she was matched against the Japanese Yoshino and Naniwa; the Yoshino was the backbone of the Japanese fleet.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang fought from the Zhiyuan, the most aggressive ship in the fleet, pitted against the Japanese Yoshino and Naniwa; the Yoshino was the core of the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 戰既酣，致遠彈將罄，世昌誓死敵。

translations.literal: As the battle grew fierce the Zhiyuan's ammunition was nearly spent; Shichang swore to die with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When the fight was hottest the Zhiyuan's shells were almost gone; Shichang vowed to die with the foe.

sentences.zh: 將士知大勢敗，陣稍亂，世昌大呼曰：「今日有死而已！

translations.literal: The officers and men knew the great trend was defeat and the formation grew slightly disorderly; Shichang shouted loudly: "Today there is nothing but death!
translations.idiomatic: The men knew the day was lost and the line wavered; Shichang roared: "Today we have only death!

sentences.zh: 然雖死而海軍聲威弗替，是即所以報國也！

translations.literal: Yet though we die, the navy's renown shall not fade—that is how we repay the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet if we die, let the navy's honor stand unbroken—that is how we serve the country!"

sentences.zh: 」眾乃定。

translations.literal: The troops then steadied.
translations.idiomatic: The crew steadied at that.

sentences.zh: 世昌遂鼓輪怒駛，欲猛觸吉野與同盡，中其魚雷，鍋船裂沉。

translations.literal: Shichang then drove the engines at full speed, intending to ram the Yoshino and perish together; he was struck by her torpedo and the boiler ship split and sank.
translations.idiomatic: Shichang ordered full ahead to ram the Yoshino and die with her; a torpedo hit him, the boiler ruptured, and the ship went down.

sentences.zh: 世昌身環氣圈不沒，汝昌及他將見之，令馳救。

translations.literal: Shichang's body was ringed by an air pocket and did not sink; Ruchang and other commanders saw this and ordered a rescue boat.
translations.idiomatic: An air pocket kept Shichang afloat; Ruchang and other officers saw it and sent a boat.

sentences.zh: 拒弗上，縮臂出圈，死之。

translations.literal: He refused to board, drew his arm from the ring, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to come aboard, slipped free of the bubble, and drowned.

sentences.zh: 其副游擊陳金揆同殉，全船二百五十人無逃者。

translations.literal: His deputy guerrilla officer Chen Jin'kui died with him; all two hundred fifty men of the ship escaped none.
translations.idiomatic: His second-in-command Chen Jinkui died beside him; not one of the ship's 250 men survived.

sentences.zh: 經遠管帶總兵林永昇、超勇管帶參將黃建寅、揚威管帶參將林履中並殞於陣。

translations.literal: The Jingyuan's commander, Commander Lin Yongsheng, the Chaoyong's Staff Captain Huang Jianyin, and the Yangwei's Staff Captain Lin Lüzhong all fell in the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Lin Yongsheng of the Jingyuan, Staff Captain Huang Jianyin of the Chaoyong, and Staff Captain Lin Lüzhong of the Yangwei all died in action.

sentences.zh: 事聞，世昌諡壯節，餘皆優恤。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, Shichang was given the posthumous title Zhuangjie; the rest were all generously compensated.
translations.idiomatic: On report of the battle Shichang received the posthumous name Zhuangjie; the others were all handsomely compensated.

sentences.zh: 世昌既死，諸船或沉或逃，遂不復成軍。

translations.literal: After Shichang's death the ships either sank or fled, and the fleet was never re-formed.
translations.idiomatic: After Shichang fell the ships sank or ran; the fleet never fought as a unit again.

sentences.zh: 世昌臨戰以忠義相激勵，死狀尤烈，世與左寶貴並稱雙忠云。

translations.literal: Shichang had roused his men with loyalty and righteousness before battle; his manner of death was especially fierce; he and Zuo Baogui were ever after called the Pair of Loyal Martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: In battle Shichang had stirred his men with talk of loyalty; his death was especially heroic; posterity paired him with Zuo Baogui as the "twin martyrs."

sentences.zh: 永昇等，忠義有傳。

translations.literal: Yongsheng and the others have their loyalty recorded elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Yongsheng and the rest have separate accounts of their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 劉步蟾，侯官人。

translations.literal: Liu Buchan was a man of Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Buchan was a native of Houguan.

sentences.zh: 幼穎異，肄業福建船政學堂，卒業試第一。

translations.literal: In youth he was exceptionally bright; he studied at the Fujian Naval Academy and ranked first in the graduation examination.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was unusually gifted; he entered the Fujian Naval Academy and graduated at the head of his class.

sentences.zh: 隸建威船，徼循南北洋資實練。

translations.literal: He served on the Jianwei and patrolled the North and South Seas to gain practical training.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to the Jianwei and cruised the northern and southern seas for hands-on experience.

sentences.zh: 同治十一年，會考閩、廣駕駛生，复冠其曹。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tongzhi he sat for the joint examination of Fujian and Guangdong navigation students and again led the field.
translations.idiomatic: In 1872 he took the joint examination of Fujian and Guangdong navigation cadets and again topped the list.

sentences.zh: 自是巡歷海岸河港，所蒞輒用​​西法測量。

translations.literal: From then on, wherever he toured coasts, rivers, and harbors, he invariably used Western methods of surveying.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter on every survey of coast, river, and port he applied Western surveying methods.

sentences.zh: 台灣地勢、番部風土尤諳習，為圖說甚晰。

translations.literal: He was especially well versed in Taiwan's terrain and the customs of the aboriginal districts, and his illustrated reports were very clear.
translations.idiomatic: He knew Taiwan's geography and aboriginal regions especially well and produced exceptionally clear illustrated reports.

sentences.zh: 光緒改元，赴歐學槍砲、水雷諸技，還留福建，敘守備。

translations.literal: When Guangxu began his reign he went to Europe to study artillery, mines, and related skills; on return he remained in Fujian and was ranked as garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Guangxu reign he studied artillery and mines in Europe; returning, he stayed in Fujian with the rank of garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 以丁寶楨、李鴻章論薦，擢游擊，會辦北洋操防。

translations.literal: On recommendation by Ding Baozhen and Li Hongzhang he was promoted to guerrilla officer and made assistant in Beiyang drill and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Ding Baozhen and Li Hongzhang, he was raised to guerrilla officer and assigned to Beiyang training and coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 十一年，赴德國購定遠艦。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he went to Germany to purchase the Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1885 he went to Germany to take delivery of the Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 維時海軍初立，借才異地，西人實為管帶，步蟾副之。

translations.literal: At that time the navy was newly founded and talent was borrowed from abroad; Westerners actually held command while Buchan served as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: The navy was new and relied on foreign expertise; Westerners nominally commanded while Buchan was second.

sentences.zh: 已而西人去，頗能舉其職。

translations.literal: After the Westerners left he was quite able to fulfill his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Once the foreigners departed he performed his duties capably.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以參將赴歐領四快船歸，遷副將，賜號強勇巴圖魯，擢右翼總兵。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, as staff captain, he went to Europe to bring back four fast cruisers; he was promoted to deputy commander, granted the title Qiangyong Batür, and made right-wing commander.
translations.idiomatic: In 1888, as staff captain, he fetched four fast cruisers from Europe; he was made deputy commander, granted Qiangyong Batür, and appointed right-wing commander.

sentences.zh: 二十年，中日戰起，海軍浮泊大東溝。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the Sino-Japanese War broke out; the navy lay at anchor in Dadonggou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1894 war with Japan began; the fleet lay at Dadonggou.

sentences.zh: 日艦至，督攝諸藝士御之，鏖戰三時許，沉敵艦三艘，運送銘軍八營，得以乘間登岸。

translations.literal: When Japanese ships arrived he directed the gunners in defense; after fierce fighting for some three hours they sank three enemy ships, and eight battalions of the Ming army were transported ashore in the interval.
translations.idiomatic: When Japanese ships appeared he directed the gun crews; after some three hours of bitter fighting three enemy vessels were sunk, and eight battalions of the Ming army were landed in the lull.

sentences.zh: 論功，晉記名提督，易其勇號曰格洪額。

translations.literal: For merit he was entered on the rolls for grand coordinator and his Batür title was changed to Gehong'e.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was entered for grand coordinator and his honorific was changed to Gehong'e.

sentences.zh: 明年，戰威海，中彈死。

translations.literal: The next year, fighting at Weihai, he was struck by a shell and died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the battle for Weihai, he was killed by gunfire.

sentences.zh: 步蟾通西學，海軍規制多出其手。

translations.literal: Buchan was versed in Western learning; much of the navy's regulations came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Buchan mastered Western naval science; much of the fleet's organization was his work.

sentences.zh: 顧喜引用鄉人，視統帥丁汝昌蔑如也，時論責其不能和衷，致僨事。

translations.literal: Yet he delighted in promoting fellow townsmen and looked down on the commander-in-chief Ding Ruchang; public opinion blamed him for failing to work in harmony and bringing about defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he favored fellow provincials and treated Admiral Ding Ruchang with contempt; critics blamed his failure to cooperate for the fleet's ruin.

sentences.zh: 然華人明海戰術，步蟾為最先，雖敗挫，殺敵甚眾。

translations.literal: Yet among Chinese who understood naval tactics, Buchan was foremost; though defeated, he killed a great many of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Among Chinese versed in naval warfare, however, Buchan stood first; though beaten, his guns inflicted heavy losses.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其忠烈，詔優恤。

translations.literal: The throne praised his loyalty and valor and ordered generous compensation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor honored his loyalty and ordered special compensation.

sentences.zh: 其左翼總兵林泰曾，亦籍侯官，同為船政學堂卒業生。

translations.literal: The left-wing commander Lin Taiceng was also registered in Houguan and was a fellow graduate of the Naval Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Left-wing commander Lin Taiceng was likewise a Houguan native and a Naval Academy graduate alongside Buchan.

sentences.zh: 管鎮遠，戰大東溝，發砲敏捷，士卒用命，撲救火彈甚力，機營砲位無少損，賜號霍春助巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He commanded the Zhenyuan; at the battle of Dadonggou he fired with agility, the soldiers obeyed orders, fought fires from incendiary shells with great effort, and the engine-room gun positions suffered no damage; he was granted the title Huochunzhu Batür.
translations.idiomatic: Commanding the Zhenyuan at Dadonggou, he fought with quick gunnery, disciplined crews, and tireless firefighting; his engine-room batteries were untouched, and he received the title Huochunzhu Batür.

sentences.zh: 駛還威海，艦觸礁受傷，憤恨蹈海死。

translations.literal: On the return voyage to Weihai the ship struck a reef and was damaged; in anger and shame he threw himself into the sea and died.
translations.idiomatic: Sailing back to Weihai his ship hit a reef; in shame and fury he drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 副將左翼中營游擊楊用霖、廣東大鵬協右營守備黃祖蓮並殉焉。

translations.literal: Deputy Commander Yang Yonglin of the left-wing central battalion guerrilla force and garrison commander Huang Zulian of the Guangdong Dapeng Right Battalion died with him.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Commander Yang Yonglin and garrison commander Huang Zulian of Dapeng perished with him.

sentences.zh: 優恤各如製。

translations.literal: Each received generous compensation according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Each was compensated according to statute.

sentences.zh: 祖蓮等，忠義有傳。

translations.literal: Zulian and the others have their loyalty recorded elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zulian and the rest have separate accounts of their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 戴宗騫，字孝侯，安徽壽州人。

translations.literal: Dai Zongqian, style name Xiaohou, was a man of Shouzhou in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Zongqian, whose style name was Xiaohou, was a native of Shouzhou in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 少以廩生治鄉團，捻酋苗沛霖數陷州，宗騫潛結各圩寨以攜貳其黨。

translations.literal: In youth, as a stipend student, he organized local militia; the Nian chieftain Miao Peilin repeatedly took the prefecture, and Zongqian secretly united the stockaded hamlets to divide his followers.
translations.idiomatic: As a young stipend scholar he raised local militia; when Nian leader Miao Peilin repeatedly seized Shouzhou, Zongqian secretly rallied the stockaded villages to turn Miao's men against one another.

sentences.zh: 同治初，謁李鴻章，上平捻十策，深器之，遂留參戎幕，積勳至知縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongzhi he called on Li Hongzhang, presented ten strategies for suppressing the Nian, and was deeply valued; he was kept on the military staff, accumulating merit until he reached the rank of magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi era he visited Li Hongzhang with ten plans to crush the Nian; Hongzhang prized him, kept him on staff, and promoted him to magistrate through accumulated service.

sentences.zh: 十一年，治南運河堤工。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he supervised dike works on the South Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In 1872 he oversaw diking on the South Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 時畿輔興水利，計臣慮餉詘，議裁兵。

translations.literal: At that time water conservancy was being promoted in the capital region; the planning ministers feared funds would run short and proposed cutting troops.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhili pushed waterworks, budget officials feared short funds and proposed troop reductions.

sentences.zh: 宗騫上書，略謂：「津沽為九河故道，漳、衛交匯，水菑衍溢。

translations.literal: Zongqian submitted a memorial, stating in summary: "Jingu is the old course of the Nine Rivers; the Zhang and Wei meet, and floodwaters spread wide.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqian memorialized in substance: "The Tianjin area lies in the old bed of the Nine Rivers; where the Zhang and Wei converge, floods spread without check.

sentences.zh: 宜闢減河洩其勢，澌枝河分其漲，俾淮、練軍治之，則兵農合一，事半而功倍。

translations.literal: It is fitting to open relief channels to release the force of the current, and branch streams to divide the flood, letting the Huai and Lian armies manage them—then soldiers and farmers unite, and the work is half done for double the effect."
translations.idiomatic: Relief rivers should be cut to bleed off pressure and branch channels to split the rise, with Huai and Lian troops doing the work—soldiers and farmers together, half the effort for twice the gain."

sentences.zh: 」鴻章以其議上聞，遂命董其役，成稻田六萬餘畝。

translations.literal: " Hongzhang forwarded his proposal to the throne and ordered him to direct the project; more than sixty thousand mu of paddy fields were completed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang sent the plan up and put Zongqian in charge; more than sixty thousand mu of rice land were brought under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 箸海上屯田志紀其事。

translations.literal: He wrote the Haishang Tuntian Zhi to record the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He recorded the project in his Haishang Tuntian Zhi (Gazetteer of Coastal Colonization).

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，中俄失和，吳大澂被命佐吉林邊務，奏宗騫自隨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu relations with Russia broke down; Wu Dacheng was ordered to assist in Jilin border affairs and memorialized that Zongqian accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1880, when relations with Russia soured, Wu Dacheng was assigned to Jilin border duty and asked that Zongqian accompany him.

sentences.zh: 大澂兼攝屯政，宗騫為治道路，築砲台，設江防，徙直、東流民，假予產業，分部護之。

translations.literal: Dacheng also held charge of colonization policy; Zongqian built roads, erected batteries, set up river defenses, moved settlers from Zhili and the east, lent them property, and posted guards by district.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng also oversaw colonization; Zongqian built roads and forts, organized river defense, resettled migrants from Zhili and the northeast, lent them land, and stationed guards by district.

sentences.zh: 塞外灌莽千里，馬賊為民患，宗騫曰：「此屯政蠹也！

translations.literal: Beyond the passes the wilds stretched a thousand li; mounted bandits plagued the people; Zongqian said: "This is the bane of colonization policy!
translations.idiomatic: A thousand li of wilderness bred mounted bandits; Zongqian declared: "This is the plague of frontier settlement!

sentences.zh: 」率將士步馳八九百里，獲渠率王林等駢誅之。

translations.literal: " He led officers and men on foot and horse for eight or nine hundred li, captured the ringleader Wang Lin and others, and executed them in a row.
translations.idiomatic: " He marched eight or nine hundred li, seized ringleader Wang Lin and his gang, and executed them in a batch.

sentences.zh: 又以緣邊荒墾，戶籍殘耗，客民渙居不相顧，因令屯聚一處，略仿內地保甲，杜絕姦宄。

translations.literal: Because the borderlands were newly opened to cultivation, household registers were depleted, and migrant settlers lived scattered without mutual aid, he ordered them to cluster in one place, roughly imitating interior baojia systems, to cut off treachery and villainy.
translations.idiomatic: With frontier registers thin and settlers scattered, he gathered them into compact settlements on the interior baojia model to suppress crime.

sentences.zh: 復設製造局、採金廠，行之期年，商民輻湊。

translations.literal: He also established manufactories and gold mines; after a year of operation merchants and people gathered in crowds.
translations.idiomatic: He founded arsenals and gold works; within a year trade and population surged.

sentences.zh: 大澂上其績狀，遷知府。

translations.literal: Dacheng reported his achievements and he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng reported his record and he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 八年，徙防洋、蒲河兩海口。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to defend the Yang and Pu River estuaries.
translations.idiomatic: In 1882 he was shifted to guard the Yang and Pu river mouths.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂歸，鴻章疏留，宗騫請終制，弗許。

translations.literal: When his mother died he returned for mourning; Hongzhang memorialized to retain him; Zongqian asked to complete the mourning period but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: On his mother's death he went home to mourn; Hongzhang asked the court to keep him in service; Zongqian pleaded to observe full mourning but was refused.

sentences.zh: 時興海軍，練水師，闢軍港，檄防威海。

translations.literal: At that time the navy was being raised, the fleet drilled, a naval base opened, and he was ordered by dispatch to defend Weihai.
translations.idiomatic: As the navy was built, sailors trained, and a naval base opened, he was ordered to Weihai's defense.

sentences.zh: 十三年，詣軍所，壁金線頂山，分鞏軍駐南岸，綏軍駐北岸。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he went to the garrison, fortified Jinxian Peak, stationed the Gong army on the south shore and the Sui army on the north.
translations.idiomatic: In 1887 he took command, fortified Jinxian Peak, and posted the Gong army south and the Sui army north.

sentences.zh: 明年，建兩岸海台各三，南曰趙北嘴、鹿角嘴、龍廟嘴，北曰北山嘴、黃泥崖、祭祀台。

translations.literal: The next year he built three coastal batteries on each shore: on the south, Zhaobeizui, Lujiaozui, and Longmiaozui; on the north, Beishanzui, Huangniya, and Jisitai.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he built three shore batteries on each side—south: Zhaobeizui, Lujiaozui, Longmiaozui; north: Beishanzui, Huangniya, Jisitai.

sentences.zh: 後路分築陸台四，南岸口較闊，更建日島地阱砲台，屹然為東防重鎮。

translations.literal: Four land batteries were built in the rear; the southern mouth being wider, a pit battery was also built on Rizhao Island; it stood as the great eastern bastion.
translations.idiomatic: Four rear land forts followed; where the southern channel was wider he added Rizhao Island's pit battery, making Weihai the eastern stronghold.

sentences.zh: 十七年，校閱海軍禮成，論功晉道員。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, when the naval review was completed, he was promoted to circuit intendant for merit.
translations.idiomatic: After the 1891 naval review he was promoted to circuit intendant for merit.

sentences.zh: 威海地瘠，士氣衰，更斥貲立義塾，延名師，至是始聞謳誦聲。

translations.literal: Weihai's soil was poor and local morale low; he spent his own funds to found a charity school and hire famous teachers, and only then did sounds of recitation begin to be heard.
translations.idiomatic: Weihai was poor and spiritless; he funded a charity school and hired noted teachers until recitation was heard in the streets.

sentences.zh: 二十年夏，日艦來攻，率師御之，傷其艦四艘，再至再敗之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twentieth year Japanese warships came to attack; he led his troops to resist, damaged four of their ships, and when they came again defeated them again.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 1894 Japanese ships attacked; he met them twice, damaging four vessels and beating them off each time.

sentences.zh: 既而旅順、大連相繼淪沒，威海勢益孤，電請北洋、山東益師，久弗應。

translations.literal: Before long Lüshun and Dalian fell in succession; Weihai's position grew more isolated; he wired the Beiyang and Shandong commands for reinforcements, but for a long time received no answer.
translations.idiomatic: Then Lüshun and Dalian fell; Weihai stood alone; he wired Beiyang and Shandong for troops but waited in vain.

sentences.zh: 其冬，連失文登、寧海。

translations.literal: That winter Wendeng and Ninghai were lost in succession.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Wendeng and Ninghai fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 時宗騫守北岸，分統劉超佩守南岸，宗騫與約，寇至互相應。

translations.literal: At that time Zongqian held the north shore while subordinate commander Liu Chaopei held the south; Zongqian agreed with him that when the enemy came they would support each other.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqian held the north bank while Liu Chaopei held the south; they pledged mutual support when attacked.

sentences.zh: 歲除，大風雪，戰橋頭集，綏軍大困，銳身救之出。

translations.literal: On New Year's Eve, in great wind and snow, they fought at Qiaotouji; the Sui army was hard pressed, and he boldly went in person to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve, in blizzard and battle at Qiaotouji, the Sui army was trapped and he charged in to pull them out.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，日軍至，輒敗去，折而南。

translations.literal: After the year turned, Japanese troops arrived, were repeatedly beaten and withdrew, then turned south.
translations.idiomatic: When the new year came Japanese troops appeared, were beaten back, then swung south.

sentences.zh: 宗騫往援，而超佩蹌踉遁，三台拱手讓敵，反訴巡撫李秉衡，誣宗騫背約。

translations.literal: Zongqian went to reinforce, but Chaopei fled in disorder; three batteries were surrendered to the enemy without a fight; he in turn reported to Governor Li Bingheng and falsely accused Zongqian of breaking their agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqian hurried to help, but Chaopei fled; three forts were handed over intact; Chaopei then told Governor Li Bingheng that Zongqian had broken their pact.

sentences.zh: 宗騫抗辯，願復三台贖罪。

translations.literal: Zongqian protested and offered to retake the three batteries to atone.
translations.idiomatic: Zongqian rebutted the charge and vowed to recover the three forts as penance.

sentences.zh: 乃募敢死士奪還二台，唯龍廟嘴未復。

translations.literal: He then recruited dare-to-die men and retook two batteries; only Longmiaozui was not recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He raised suicide squads and retook two forts; only Longmiaozui remained in enemy hands.

sentences.zh: 日軍倏大集，二台仍不守，宗騫退歸，登祭祀台。

translations.literal: Japanese troops suddenly massed in force; the two batteries still could not be held; Zongqian withdrew and mounted Jisitai.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese concentrated in strength; the two forts fell again; Zongqian fell back to Jisitai.

sentences.zh: 所部卒譁變，宗騫佯弗省，行數武，槍齊發，材官追斬一人，眾散走。

translations.literal: His troops mutinied; Zongqian pretended not to notice; after a few paces guns fired together; a sergeant pursued and cut down one man, and the crowd scattered.
translations.idiomatic: His men mutinied; he feigned ignorance; a few steps on, rifles crashed; a sergeant cut down one ringleader and the rest fled.

sentences.zh: 宗騫既登，乃無一從者。

translations.literal: Once Zongqian had mounted the battery, not a single man followed him.
translations.idiomatic: On the rampart he stood utterly alone.

sentences.zh: 夜宿藥庫，丁汝昌詣籌戰守策，宗騫曰：「綏、鞏軍已西去，孤台危棘，恐資敵。

translations.literal: At night he lodged in the powder magazine; Ding Ruchang came to discuss attack and defense; Zongqian said: "The Sui and Gong armies have already gone west; the isolated batteries are perilous and may arm the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: That night in the magazine Ding Ruchang sought plans; Zongqian said: "The Sui and Gong forces have marched west; these lone forts are doomed and will only arm the foe.

sentences.zh: 」汝昌令毀台，強掖之下。

translations.literal: " Ruchang ordered the batteries destroyed and had men forcibly escort him down.
translations.idiomatic: " Ruchang ordered the works blown and had him dragged down by force.

sentences.zh: 宗騫念南北各有地阱台，此其勢尚可為，乃詣劉公島就副將張德山。

translations.literal: Zongqian reflected that north and south each had pit batteries and the position might still be tenable; he therefore went to Liugong Island to see Deputy Commander Zhang Deshan.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering pit batteries on both shores, he crossed to Liugong Island to seek Deputy Commander Zhang Deshan.

sentences.zh: 德山無戰守志，宗騫飲金死，威海師遂熸。

translations.literal: Deshan had no will to fight or hold; Zongqian drank gold and died, and the Weihai garrison was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Deshan would neither fight nor hold; Zongqian took poison; Weihai's land defense was finished.

sentences.zh: 鴻章以死事聞，詔優恤。

translations.literal: Hongzhang reported his death in battle and the court ordered generous compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang reported him killed in duty and the court ordered special compensation.

sentences.zh: 復以秉衡請，贈太常寺卿。

translations.literal: On Bingheng's request he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At Bingheng's request he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 論曰：中東之戰，陸軍皆遁，寶貴獨死平壤；

translations.literal: The commentator says: In the war between China and Japan, the land armies all fled, but Baogui alone died at Pyongyang;
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: In the Sino-Japanese War every land army ran, yet Baogui alone died at Pyongyang;

sentences.zh: 海軍皆降，世昌獨死東溝。

translations.literal: the navy all surrendered, but Shichang alone died at Dadonggou.
translations.idiomatic: every naval unit surrendered, yet Shichang alone died at Dadonggou.

sentences.zh: 中外傳其壯節，並稱「雙忠」。

translations.literal: Chinese and foreigners alike spread word of their heroic deaths, jointly calling them the "Pair of Loyal Martyrs."
translations.idiomatic: At home and abroad their deaths were hailed as heroic; together they were called the "twin martyrs."

sentences.zh: 及日兵入奉，永山獨死鳳城，敵遂長驅進矣。

translations.literal: When Japanese troops entered Fengtian, Yong Shan alone died at Fengcheng, and the enemy then drove straight in.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese entered Fengtian, Yong Shan alone fell at Fengcheng—and the enemy marched on unopposed.

sentences.zh: 旅、大既失，威海勢孤，步蟾、宗騫皆先後誓死。

translations.literal: After Lüshun and Dalian were lost, Weihai stood isolated; Buchan and Zongqian each in turn swore to die.
translations.idiomatic: With Lüshun and Dalian gone, Weihai was cut off; Buchan and Zongqian each pledged his life.

sentences.zh: 士氣如此，豈遂不可一戰？

translations.literal: With morale such as this, could they truly not have fought one more battle?
translations.idiomatic: Morale like this—was there truly no fight left in them?

sentences.zh: 此主兵者之責。

translations.literal: That was the responsibility of those who commanded the armies.
translations.idiomatic: The fault lay with those who held the armies' command.

sentences.zh: 五人雖敗，猶有榮焉！

translations.literal: Though these five men were defeated, they still had honor!
translations.idiomatic: These five men were beaten, yet their honor stands!
